Change B's test creates articles with an already-lowercase tag, which remains valid under A. Change A's test filters with lowercase 'dragons', which B leaves unchanged. rows.explanation: Change B adds a 60s in-memory cache for GET /api/tags and invalidates it only when tags are added (article creation). Change A makes article deletion also delete orphaned tags from the database, but nothing in A invalidates the cache. After merge: a client calls GET /api/tags (cache populated with ["solo","shared"]), then an article is deleted and the 'solo' tag is removed from the DB; GET /api/tags continues to return 'solo' for up to 60 seconds. B's cache assumes tags only change on creation (its doc says 'Call it whenever tags are added'), and A breaks that assumption by removing tags. Neither change alone is wrong, but together the tags endpoint serves stale, deleted tags.

Change B's new userChangePassword controller already hashes the new password with hashPassword before calling userUpdatePrisma. Merged, the new endpoint double-hashes: userUpdatePrisma hashes the already-hashed value, so the stored password is hash(hash(newPassword)). After changing the password via POST /api/user/password, login with the new password compares against a double hash and fails (403), locking the user out of the new password. B's tests only check that the stored value differs from plain text and the old hash, so they still pass. A's tests only exercise PUT /api/user, so they pass too.

The schema edits are in different lines and merge cleanly, and the existing tests don't check updatedAt after a read.
